Pānui and hui collateral

One notice, four formats, no rebuild

Every hui has the same six facts. I set them out once as fields, then lay them into a member pānui, an A4 notice, an event banner and social tiles, so nothing has to be retyped and nothing can disagree.

FieldsKaupapaTe rā (date)Te wā (time)Te wāhi (venue)Ko wai (who is welcome)Kōrero mai (contact)

Member pānui

The one thing members most need to know sits first, in two lines, with one button. Everything else sits below it in short blocks. Plain English with te reo headings.

Hui notice, A4

The six fields as rows, big enough to read across a room. The same file exports as a PDF for email, a print for a noticeboard, or a post.

Te rā
Date, written out in full
Te wā
Start and finish
Te wāhi
Venue and town
Ko wai
Who is invited, in plain words
Kōrero mai
Phone or email, one only

Event banner

A wide layout for a Facebook cover or a screen at the door. The name leads, and the three facts people look for sit in one block at the right so they are never hunted for.

Social tiles, three squares

A question, then the ask, then how to answer. Square tiles work in a Facebook post and an Instagram grid. The type is large enough to read on a phone held at arm's length.

Size
1080 × 1080 px
Order
Hook, question, how to answer

All four are templates with bracketed fields. They contain no logos, no taonga and no people. Unofficial sample, not published by Te Rūnanga-Ā-Iwi-O-Ngāpuhi. Anything with te reo or tikanga in it is checked with the right people before it goes out.

Content calendar

A four week rhythm, and six months around it

A calendar is a promise about what goes out, when, and who checked it. Filter by channel, or pick any item to see its brief. Dates and items are placeholders, not the rūnanga's plans.

My proposed six months

How I would set the job up, from a 13 January 2027 start or earlier. This is a plan, not past work.

  1. Month 1Listen

    Read the last pānui and posts. List every channel and login. Agree what must be checked, and by whom, before anything goes out.

  2. Month 2Templates

    Pānui, hui notice, banner, tiles and a 15 second reel, as files the team can fill in.

  3. Month 3Library

    Sort images and video into one library, named the same way, with a note on who agreed to what.

  4. Month 4Calendar runs

    The four week rhythm goes live, with a check step before every send.

  5. Month 5First reports

    One page a month: reach, engagement, the best three posts, one thing to change.

  6. Month 6Handover

    A written plan, so the team can run all of it without me.

Past work: New Image

How my New Image work was done, in three diagrams.

The real work belongs to New Image's clients, so I rebuilt it as diagrams.

Email newsletters

Every newsletter waits for approval before it goes out.

A brief becomes an email, is checked against the brand rules, and goes out only once someone approves it. I built 38 and 31 went out.

Overview

One newsletter

A brief becomes an email and is checked before it goes out. Tap a step to see it.

  1. Write the brief Each email newsletter starts as one brief and one set of content.
  2. Build the email The email is built from one template with one text file per language: English, Chinese and Bahasa Malaysia.
  3. Brand check The draft is checked against the brand rules before it is uploaded to Moosend.
  4. Approval Every draft waits for approval before it goes out.
Countries

The right pack in every country

One post becomes one image per country, showing that country's product pack and language.

Needs a native speaker

Overview

16 countries

A table picks the language and the official product pack for each country. Tap the post, a country or the total.

  1. One post The post is built once.
  2. Sixteen countries The tool holds each country's language and official product pack. A country that needs a line from a native speaker is marked.
  3. The total 16 countries, each with its own language and product pack.
Build and review

Built by a program, checked on a review page

Posts are built from a list, then sent to a review page where all the notes come back in one place.

Review page
Checked again

Overview

Four steps

Posts are built from a list and sent to a review page. Tap a step to see what happens there.

  1. The program builds posts A program builds posts, carousels and reels from a list of the posts to make, so I do not build each by hand.
  2. The team checks them The team checks each post on phone or desktop and leaves notes.
  3. Notes go back together The notes come back together, and the posts are fixed.
  4. Approved posts Approved posts are ready to publish.

How I work

Plan, make, publish, measure.

How I would work with you: four steps, repeated each month.

  1. Plan

    A content calendar for each month, set out by channel, with pānui, hui and rangatahi posts placed against the dates that matter to members.

  2. Make

    Templates in Canva, short video in CapCut, written in plain English. A fluent reader checks any te reo before it is used.

  3. Publish

    Member pānui, website, social and email. Each item goes through a review check before it goes out, with notes sent back in one go.

  4. Measure

    Reach and engagement, looked at each month, in a one⁠-⁠page report.
